What makes Triceratops so amazing?

With three horns on its face and a big frill (neck shield), Triceratops is a herbivore dinosaur that kids adore. Its name even means "three-horned face."

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Triceratops

Triceratops lived about 66 million years ago at the end of the Cretaceous period and was around 7.9-9m long. It's known for its three horns—one above the nose and two above the eyes—and the big frill at the back of its head. The horns and frill helped ward off predators like T. rex, but modern research suggests their more important role was likely as display and mating signals.

Points worth exploring together

Point out things like the three horns (above the nose and eyes), the big frill, defense against predators, and display signals. Talking about "Why did it have horns and a frill?" together is a great way to spark curiosity.

Parent guide — how to grow curiosity

Point to and count the horns with your finger (1 on the nose, 2 above the eyes). Compare with a photo of a rhinoceros, and mention "It probably showed off to its friends with its horns (display)" to make it even more exciting.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How many horns does Triceratops have?
A. Three in total—one above the nose and two above the eyes. Its name even means "three-horned face."

Q. What were the horns and frill used for?
A. They helped ward off predators, but the view that display and mating signals were their more important role is widely favored.

Q. How can we enjoy it at home?
A. Counting the horns by pointing to their positions and comparing it with a rhinoceros are great activities.
